chunks: And from al-Ṣaffār, from al-Sindī ibn Muḥammad, from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: What is the wudu (ablution) that Allah has made obligatory upon the servants for one who has come from relieving himself or has urinated? He said: He washes his private part, removes the feces, then performs wudu (ablution), two times each.

key_terms.افْتَرَضَهُ: made obligatory or prescribed as a duty
key_terms.الْغَائِطِ: feces or the act of defecation
key_terms.الْوُضُوءُ: the ritual ablution required for purification before acts of worship

ai.seo_question: What wudu (ablution) is required after urinating or defecating according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith asks Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام about the obligatory wudu (ablution) for one who has relieved himself or urinated. He explains the required purification by washing the private part, cleaning away the feces, and then performing wudu (ablution) with a repeated washing pattern mentioned as two times each.
